clue.text: Disastrous time — smoker may have this rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for what a smoker has is read backwards

parts.note: a smoker may well have a cigar in hand

explanation.surface: A smoker turning down a cigar at a bad moment, as if disaster struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disastrous is calamitous, the sense of a sad, catastrophic outcome as in a drama.

clue.text: Ruse dismissing American demand for salvage

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the letters for American are removed from the word ruse

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American
to claim is to demand as one's right

explanation.surface: A trick is set aside while someone insists on salvaging something.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing US from RUSE leaves RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to recover it from waste or loss, a synonym of winning it back.

clue.text: Playing on errors may reveal a hopeless case

indicators.note: to reveal is to uncover, so the letters sit concealed within the phrase playing on errors

explanation.surface: A player who keeps making mistakes shows they are past saving.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone doomed or beyond help is called a write-off, a person who is finished.

clue.text: Picture of small headland found south of Newcastle, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so these letters follow the city

parts.note: Newcastle is an example of a city in northern England
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A painting of a little promontory just south of Newcastle on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cityscape is a picture or view of an urban scene, by analogy with landscape.

clue.text: Uninspired by prisoner becoming full of remorse

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
trite means hackneyed and uninspired

explanation.surface: A dull inmate comes to feel sorry for what they did.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite describes someone penitent, feeling sincere regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Nurses perhaps must cover five such chairs

definitions.note: plural chairs matching the plural answer

indicators.note: to cover is to enclose, so the carers word wraps round the Roman numeral

parts.note: nurses are an example of carers
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Nurses having to put covers on five chairs of a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such' points back at the clue: carvers are the kind of chairs the wordplay produces.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver is a dining chair with arms, traditionally used by the person carving the meat.

clue.text: Animal discovered in many a lake

indicators.note: discovered in means found within, so the letters lie concealed in the run many a lake

explanation.surface: A creature found in many lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a southern African antelope, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Stress check on behalf of discontented comrade

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
for means on behalf of, as in speaking for someone

indicators.note: dis-contented means with the contents removed, so only the outer letters of comrade remain

explanation.surface: Pressure from checking up for a disgruntled fellow worker.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to emphasise or strengthen it, a synonym of bolstering.

clue.text: Move into net savings scheme

indicators.note: move signals that the letters of into net are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to transfer money into a net savings plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is an annuity scheme where subscribers pool money and survivors' shares grow as others die.

clue.text: Business people must hold back alarm

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the word for people encloses the word for back

parts.note: a nation is a people
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Company staff have to suppress their panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation is dismay or anxiety, a synonym of alarm in the sense of fright.

clue.text: Left an angry European game

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, a form of an
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A cross European walks off from a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks, an example of a game.

clue.text: Female just after a fling

indicators.note: after means placed later, so the letters for female and just come behind a

parts.note: fair means just, even-handed

explanation.surface: A woman who wants only a brief romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A fling is a short romantic relationship, the same as a liaison or dalliance.

clue.text: Spear mostly used with a creature from Africa

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for spear is dropped

parts.note: to impale is to spear, pierce with a point

explanation.surface: Hunting an African beast with a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope, so an example of a creature from that continent.

clue.text: Program needing time to include objective for attachment

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so the program and time words enclose the objective

parts.note: an app is a computer program
an age is a long period of time
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: Software that needs time to incorporate a target before it can attach something.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or attached to a larger thing, such as a limb.

clue.text: Curses seeing bottle's no answer on board ship

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so the shortened courage sits between the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: no signals the letter for answer is absent from the word for nerve

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or nerve; the clue reads bottle has

explanation.surface: Sailors swear when the ship's bottle offers no solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a cause of great suffering, like a curse or affliction.

clue.text: Rule exercised by limited company?

parts.note: a limited company suggests a business, but read literally it is a small group of people who hold power

explanation.surface: A question about governance in a limited liability firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by a small elite few is the meaning, the limited company being that small set.

clue.text: Lies from women needing jumpers

parts.note: hoppers are things that jump, such as fleas or grasshoppers

explanation.surface: Untruths from women who want sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like British sweaters but means creatures that leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoppers is slang for big lies, outrageous fibs.

clue.text: New vehicles with no source of vacuum coils

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are remade in a fresh order
with no means lacking, so the initial of vacuum is removed from vehicles
the source of a word is its beginning, its first letter

explanation.surface: Fresh vehicles running without vacuum-driven coils.
explanation.walkthrough: VEHICLES without V leaves EHICLES, which 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Helices is the plural of helix, a spiral or coil shape.

clue.text: Stealth needed by some losing heart before battle in France

indicators.note: before places the letters from some ahead of the battle
losing heart means the middle letters are dropped, leaving only the ends of some

parts.note: Crecy was a 1346 battle in northern France won by the English

explanation.surface: Some soldiers lose their nerve before a French battle and need stealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrecy is concealment, keeping things hidden, close to the idea of stealth.

clue.text: Period that is needed to cover church silver

indicators.note: to cover is to wrap around, so the that-is letters enclose church and silver

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
CE stands for Church of England
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A time when the church's silver must be covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice age is a geological period of glaciation, an era.

clue.text: Discovered area described by fabulous legend

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the jumbled letters go round the area letter
fabulous suggests something fantastical, so the letters of legend are made into a fantasy arrangement

explanation.surface: Land found as told in a mythical legend.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to gather information bit by bit, so gleaned means found out.

clue.text: This may be taken as commitment

definitions.text: This may be taken as commitment

parts.words: This may be taken as commitment
parts.note: the idiom take the dive into something means to commit decisively to a course of action

explanation.surface: Something accepted as a pledge.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom about taking a decisive leap, meaning to commit oneself boldly.

clue.text: Weariness regularly seen in audit

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of seen in audit is taken

explanation.surface: Tiredness commonly observed during an accounts check.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and tiredness, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Cleaner with a dress, oddly, will be game

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth of dress

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady with a strange outfit makes it a fun occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party game where players act out words for others to guess.

clue.text: A newly-wed has no right to stand

indicators.note: has no means lacking, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly wed

explanation.surface: A recently married person has no right to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to tolerate, as in can't stand someone, a synonym of bear.

clue.text: Series of events caused by a car on thin ice crashing

indicators.note: crashing suggests a smash, so the letters of a car on thin ice are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pile-up begins when a car skids on thin ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain reaction is a sequence of events, each causing the next.

clue.text: Bitterness seen since shame engulfs Her Majesty

parts.note: as can mean since, because

indicators.note: engulfs means swallows up, so the word for shame surrounds the royal letters

parts.note: pity means shame, as in what a shame
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Resentment arises because a scandal swallows the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Asperity is harshness of tone or manner, a sharp bitterness.

clue.text: Submits returns

definitions.meaning: profits or produces, as an investment does

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gives way and gives a profit, as land or shares produce income.
